area: files, browser and integrations (apps/server/src/files, agent/browser, core/browser, integrations/composio and kernel)
purpose: Give agents a shared chat and drive filesystem with safe concurrent writes, a bash shell over it, a real browser on the user's Kernel browser, and connected-app tools through Composio.
summary: The file index, upload and download paths, and the Kernel and Composio key handling are sound and well tested. The gaps are one false promise (bash says one command is one transaction, but a command spanning chat files, drive or soul commits each space separately), a tab-cap race in the browser connection, and a browser capability spread over four layers with stacked decision strategies and experiment scripts that have no caller.

subareas.name: room, home and soul file backends + FileIndex
subareas.why: Expect-sha check runs inside the row-write transaction, and R2 deletes happen after commit. withMount.commit (room-fs.ts:627-630) and withSoul.commit (room-fs.ts:698-701) commit one space, then the next, so a later refusal leaves the earlier space written.

subareas.name: bash emulator
subareas.why: just-bash plus a ~260-line CommandFs adapter is the right size. Network, python and javascript are off (bash.ts:406), so bash cannot reach the outside. MAX_READS comment (bash.ts:13) conflicts with AGENTS.md on the Free budget. A full recursive room listing runs on every command (bash.ts:142).

subareas.name: upload, download, pending
subareas.why: Keys come from the session user id, downloads set sandbox CSP and nosniff, and size and MIME checks are at the edge. usedBytes lists every R2 object of the user on each upload (upload.ts refuse and complete). pending.ts repeats upload.ts multipart and name code.

subareas.name: agent browser: connection, tools, tools-more, lease port, deciders
subareas.why: room() awaits lease.state() before counting tabs, and borrow() registers tabs only after openTab resolves, so parallel browse calls can overrun the 8-tab cap. Four tab-state maps and eleven browser tools. Egress wiring for the deciders is correct (agent-do.ts:320, deciders.ts jevPort).

subareas.name: core/browser: cdp, page, plan, decide, worker
subareas.why: A decision goes through a heuristic fast path, the model decider, Jev, and an escalate wrapper, with two rankers. Three word-overlap scorers (candidates.ts, summary.ts, rank.ts). session.ts wraps one WebSocket in Effect Scope and callback plumbing.

subareas.name: core/browser scripts
subareas.why: No package.json script, no importer, no doc reference. Four one-off experiments, 686 lines, that read dev keys and make live model calls.

subareas.name: kernel integration
subareas.why: reapDecision is a pure table, the single-flight queue serialises browser creation, the key is sealed with AAD and never logged, and the CDP URL goes only to the asking agent. Dev hooks are gated by devOnly (user/dev.ts).

subareas.name: composio integration
subareas.why: Session URL origin is checked, so the key only goes to Composio. Learned direct tools add a candidates map, a classify call per learned tool, a stale-while-revalidate listing cache and generation counters. Fetches run from UserDO with global fetch, not egress.

strengths: Optimistic writes: the expect-sha check and row write share one transactionSync (file-index.ts put), so two writers cannot lose an update.
R2 hygiene: superseded and removed objects are deleted after commit (applyFs, dropAfter), and a failed commit deletes the objects it stored.
Bash cannot reach the network: the Bash constructor sets no network option (bash.ts:406).
Downloads are served with CSP sandbox and nosniff; upload keys come only from the session user id.
Kernel and Composio keys are sealed with AAD and never put in errors; the Composio session URL must be on its own origin.
Kernel reap policy and switch order (delete before create) are pure and tested.

Test coverage is broad: bash.test.ts (23), room-fs, files, attachments, kernel-lease (22), kernel-files, composio-tools (27), browser-tools, browser-connection, and five core/browser test files with a fake CDP.

problems.title: Bash's one-transaction promise is false across spaces
problems.evidence: room-fs.ts:627-630 commits chat files, then the drive (user DO); room-fs.ts:698-701 commits the rest, then soul.set. bash.ts:382-386 says nothing in one space was saved, which is false for a space that already committed. Tool text at extensions/files.ts:201 promises one transaction; bash.test.ts:291 covers only success.
problems.fix: Refuse a command that writes to more than one space, or state per-space commits in the tool text and error. Add a test where the drive write is refused.

problems.title: Parallel browse calls can overrun the tab cap
problems.evidence: connection.ts room() awaits lease.state() before checking the count; borrow() and openHeld() register tabs only after openTab resolves. Two parallel calls both pass. browser-connection.test.ts tests only a sequential ninth tab.
problems.fix: Reserve the count before the first await, release on failure, and add a concurrent-borrow test.

problems.title: Composio and browser fetches may sit outside the egress rule
problems.evidence: AGENTS.md: an agent's run fetches the outside only through egress. composio/client.ts composioRpc and callTool use global fetch from UserDO for every connected-app call a run makes; kernel/connect.ts fetchPage sends browser_fetch URLs to Kernel curl. architecture.md section 27 notes the CDP socket as a DEVIATION and does not cover these.
problems.fix: Decide whether these count as the outside. If so, route them through egress. Either way, write the decision in architecture.md.

problems.title: bash subrequest budget contradicts AGENTS.md
problems.evidence: bash.ts:13 says Free allows 1,000 subrequests; bash.ts:14 sets MAX_READS=400. AGENTS.md and architecture.md:932 say 50. A web search found R2 binding calls count as subrequests, but Cloudflare's Free numbers conflict (50 on the limits page, 1,000 for services in a Feb 2026 changelog). UNVERIFIED for a DO invocation.
problems.fix: Measure the R2 limit inside a DO invocation as architecture.md:932 did for fetch, then fix the comment and MAX_READS.

problems.title: Every upload lists all of the user's R2 objects
problems.evidence: upload.ts usedBytes pages through bucket.list on every putOne, create and complete. Each page is one R2 subrequest, so cost grows with the user's file count.
problems.fix: Keep a running byte total in UserDO, updated on commit and delete.

problems.title: setTimeout inside Durable Object code
problems.evidence: cdp/browser.ts:33 auto-dismisses a dialog by timer; kernel/lease.ts:60 and composio/limit.ts:40 sleep in-request; page/act.ts:97 is the wait step. AGENTS.md forbids setTimeout to schedule work in a DO. The dialog timer is the only scheduling one, and it dies with the CDP socket.
problems.fix: Expire the dialog hold on the next browser call instead of by timer, or note the risk.

problems.title: Full room listing on every bash command
problems.evidence: bash.ts:142 CommandFs.open calls files.list('/', true) and loads every file row into memory, per command, with no count cap.
problems.fix: Read directories lazily as the emulator asks. Not urgent.

problems.title: Dead migration shim
problems.evidence: composio/store.ts:21-22 deletes pre-session rows, documented 'until 2026-10-11', which is today, and runs on every construction.
problems.fix: Delete the two lines once no production row lacks a session.

overengineering.title: Browser capability spans four layers
overengineering.evidence: agent/browser/connection.ts (262) + agent/browser/lease.ts (74) + integrations/kernel/lease.ts (270) + user/kernel-wiring.ts + core/browser/src/cdp (319). LeasePort exists largely to be mocked.
overengineering.why: The UserDO hop is a documented choice (architecture 27.1). Merge LeasePort into connection.ts when either file is next edited.

overengineering.title: Effect wrapper around one WebSocket
overengineering.evidence: core/browser/src/cdp/session.ts (177) uses Effect.callback, Scope, acquireRelease and timeoutOrElse for request/response over one socket.
overengineering.why: A Promise version is about 90 lines with the same timeouts. Change it only when session.ts is touched for another reason.

overengineering.title: Four decision strategies and three word scorers
overengineering.evidence: plan/fast.ts, decide/model.ts, decide/jev.ts, decide/escalate.ts, plus rank.ts lexical and Jev rankers; word scorers in candidates.ts, summary.ts and rank.ts.
overengineering.why: Keep Jev and escalate.ts (cost story) and the fast path (saves model calls). Merge the three word scorers into words.ts.

overengineering.title: Experiment scripts with no caller
overengineering.evidence: core/browser/scripts: decide-probe.ts (124), jev-ab.ts (59), probe.ts (118), bench.ts (385). No package.json entry, no importer, no doc reference.
overengineering.why: They answered their questions. Recover bench.ts from git history if it is needed again.

overengineering.title: Duplicate sealed-key stores
overengineering.evidence: integrations/composio/store.ts and integrations/kernel/store.ts each implement the same sealed key row, reseal rule and generation counter.
overengineering.why: The risk is the two reseal rules drifting. Extract one helper when either changes.

overengineering.title: Two parallel upload paths
overengineering.evidence: files/upload.ts (room file writes) and files/pending.ts (message attachments) each repeat multipart create, part and complete, and the name check.
overengineering.why: Different purposes, so both stay. Share the helpers when either changes.

overengineering.title: Eleven browser tools
overengineering.evidence: tools.ts registers five; tools-more.ts registers six. BROWSER_RULES spends prompt text on which to use.
overengineering.why: browser_extract and browser_look overlap browse. Cutting tools is a product call; measure selection errors first.

overengineering.title: Composio learned-tool cache
overengineering.evidence: composio/connect.ts candidates map, per-tool classify, listing cache, generation counters.
overengineering.why: It saves a search turn each chat and has 27 tests.

overengineering.title: room-fs virtual spaces (withMount, withSoul)
overengineering.evidence: room-fs.ts:571-705, each wrapped once in agent-do.ts:329-331.
overengineering.why: Single-caller wrappers, but they put /home and /me in one tree and are tested. The problem is the commit, not the layering.

tests: apps/server/test: bash.test.ts, room-fs.test.ts, files.test.ts, attachments.test.ts, delete-files.test.ts, kernel-files.test.ts, kernel-lease.test.ts, kernel-browser-state.test.ts, browser-connection.test.ts, browser-tools.test.ts, composio-tools.test.ts, composio-limit.test.ts, spill.test.ts, work-tools.test.ts. core/browser/test: browser, plan, session, tabs, worker (fake CDP). CLI verify suites: bash, file-tools, files, attachments, browser, browser-takeover, browser-run, kernel, composio, composio-extension, room-search. Gaps: no cross-space partial-commit test, no concurrent tab-cap test, no file-count or read-limit check against the real Free budget. The scripts have no tests.
